title: STATE
subtitle: State Design Collective
description: A platform for designers to post work at any stage, get and give constructive feedback, and build your reputation within the community.

sections.label: Problem
sections.heading: Real Designs Need Real Feedback
sections.body: Designers can't work in a vacuum. They need honest critique on their work.

sections.label: Research
sections.heading: Likes don't Translate to Good Design
sections.body: There is no dedicated app for deign critiques. Behance, Reddit, and Instagram promote algorithms for likes not feedback. The design community deserves a better way to critique work.

sections.label: Proposition
sections.heading: A Platform Built for Designers
sections.body: With the ever-evolving digital world and it's rapidly changing standards, STATE needs to include all design disciplines and all methods for sharing content. Users can upload any file type from Figma prototypes to video files, to 3D models.

sections.label: Solution
sections.heading: A Gated System that Rewards Constructive Feedabck
sections.body: Rather than posting projects for likes, users get scored for project posting and critiquing. posting a project requires enough crit score which creates a nurturing community around sharing work as well as feedback.

title: Zira
subtitle: Production Dashboard for Industrial Manufacturers
description: Led marketing and branding initiatives while contributing to computer vision AI modeling for a production analytics dashboard.

sections.label: Problem
sections.heading: Manufacturing plants are either struggling to get metrics on production or are drowning in spreadsheets of data.
sections.body: Manufacturers like lumber yards are running machines all day and are content counting production by hand even though there are more efficient methods.

sections.label: Question
sections.heading: Users don't like change.
sections.body: How do you convince a blue collar industry that an AI technology can help them produce more?

sections.label: Research
sections.heading: I spent time on the factory floor before opening Figma.
sections.body: We stood with line operators to understand their actual workflow: how they scanned for issues, what caused them to act, and where current processes fell short.

sections.label: Proposition
sections.heading: Design for users not for yourself
sections.body: This perspective let me design not just what metrics looks good on a monitor, but for what the operators actually needed to see.

sections.label: Solution
sections.heading: A dashboard built for the factory floor.
sections.body: The resulting dashboard featured customizable alert hierarchies, camera feed integration, and metric summaries tested with operators in real production environments. The brand and marketing site built alongside it positioned Zira as a credible enterprise product in a growing industrial market.

title: Plan With CoCo
subtitle: AI Wedding Planning Assistant
description: Built the full technical infrastructure and led UX design for an AI-powered wedding planning platform. From architecture decisions to user testing and deployment.

items: Auto help-desk ticket generation via LLM

sections.label: Problem
sections.heading: Wedding planning as a couple can be stressful.
sections.body: Couples face a wall of decisions with no roadmap: From finding venues to napkin rentals, most couples don't know what they don't know, and the tools available are spreadsheets, Pinterest boards, generic apps.

sections.label: Question
sections.heading: What if planning your wedding felt like talking to someone who'd done it before?
sections.body: The core question wasn't 'how do we organize wedding tasks?' it was 'how do we make couples feel confident and connected from day one?' That reframe shifted the product from a productivity tool to a guided experience.

sections.label: Research
sections.heading: We mapped the full planning journey before writing a line of code.
sections.body: I conducted user interviews with recently married couples to map where stress peaked, where decisions clustered, and what information people wished they'd had earlier.

sections.label: Proposition
sections.heading: AI deals with complexity but we handle the emotions.
sections.body: Large language models generate personalized timelines, vendor shortlists, and budget breakdowns based on each couple's inputs. But the interface needed to feel human, conversational, unhurried, and emotionally aware of what this moment means in someone's life. That meant listening to peoples stories and designing an app that helps couples through the process instead of overloading them with AI slop.

sections.label: Solution
sections.heading: A big decision requires a lot of research
sections.body: The outcome is a resource that helps couples research vendors and ideas, compile them into a handoff sheet for wedding coordinators, and prepare for their wedding days.

title: Apex Semi (now Cadence)
subtitle: Dashboard for Batch Computing Software
description: Created a customer-facing Django dashboard with LDAP security integration for a semiconductor company. Apex Semi was acquired by Cadence Design Systems in 2024.

items: Lead user interviews to drive new features
Develop front and back end features

sections.label: Problem
sections.heading: Enterprise licensing dashboards were built for IT teams, not chip engineers.
sections.body: Apex Semi's customers — engineers at major semiconductor companies — needed access to complex licensing and analytics data. The existing tooling was either too generic or too opaque. Trust is hard to build when the interface doesn't speak your users' language.

sections.label: Question
sections.heading: How do you design for engineers who understand the system better than you do?
sections.body: Chip engineers are precise, skeptical of unnecessary UI chrome, and accustomed to dense data. The question wasn't 'how do we make this approachable?' — it was 'how do we make this credible and efficient for people who will notice every wrong decision?'

sections.label: Research
sections.heading: The data model and the design co-evolved.
sections.body: I worked closely with the backend team from day one — not after the API was built. By understanding the licensing data model as it was being designed, I could make UI decisions that made sense for how the data actually behaved, not how I wished it would.

sections.label: Proposition
sections.heading: Match the density of the data with the precision of the interface.
sections.body: The design language was deliberate and restrained: no unnecessary visual decoration, clear information hierarchy, and role-based views that surface only what each user type needs. Security wasn't bolted on — it was woven into every interaction through the LDAP integration.

sections.label: Solution
sections.heading: Secure, precise, and proven — acquired by Cadence.
sections.body: The dashboard shipped with enterprise-grade LDAP authentication, giving clients role-based access to their licensing and analytics data. Apex Semi was acquired by Cadence Design Systems in 2024, validating the product's technical foundation and the quality of the work that went into it.

title: Slate Auto
subtitle: EV Auto App Design
description: 3 day design sprint to create a concept for an electric vehicle app focused on user experience and branding.

sections.label: Problem
sections.heading: New modes of transportation require new interfaces.
sections.body: Electric vehicle drivers not only expect, but rely on a high level of technology in their automotive products. Although Slate position's itself as the affordable truck, it still needs to meet these high standards.

sections.label: Question
sections.heading: What would an EV app look like if it was designed with the same attention to personality and affordability as the truck?
sections.body: How might Slate design a mobile-first experience that reinforces confidence at every interaction while maintaining the minimalist Slate aesthetic?

sections.label: Research
sections.heading: Three days to research, audit, design, and finalize
sections.body: After defining the project guidelines and sprint deadlines, deep research on Slate's competitors revealed EV owner's pain points with flagship electric vehicles.

sections.label: Proposition
sections.heading: Every interaction should reduce friction, and build trust
sections.body: The app needed to lead with the most relevant information and shift as the user journey progressed. I proposed a single-surface dashboard that adapts to the driver's context depending on the proximity t the truck.

sections.label: Solution
sections.heading: Bold, minimal, and unmistakably Slate.
sections.body: The visual design mirrors the truck's industrial identity: monochrome palette, heavy typography, and confident negative space. I built a high-fidelity Figma prototype that demonstrates the core flows.

title: nib
subtitle: Task Tracking Mobile App
description: A Bullet Journal inspired task tracking mobile application that lets users write, erase, and cross off tasks day by day.

items: Write, erase, and cross off tasks
Aspirations list to keep users motivated

sections.label: Problem
sections.heading: Smart phones are less productive
sections.body: Our personal smart phones are becoming less and less productive as home pages become cluttered with apps.

sections.label: Question
sections.heading: What does a home page really need?
sections.body: How can we transform home pages to keep phone user's focused rather than reaching for apps to doom scroll?

sections.label: Proposition
sections.heading: A simple widget with simple feedback
sections.body: Replacing home screen apps with an intuitive task racker that motivates users based on their aspirations and habits.

sections.label: Solution
sections.heading: All you need is a nib
sections.body: Nib lets users write, erase, and cross off tasks day by day.
